=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2047-2053 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The workflow’s timeout/polling defaults differ from the README values, so the collector waits far less and polls less often than documented.
  WHY: The reviewer reported `CHECK_RUNS_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECS 120 vs 1200` and `CHECK_RUNS_POLL_INTERVAL_SECS 30 vs 20`, which changes runtime behavior and lowers the chance of capturing failed check-run logs in time.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2053-2053 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The surrounding comments still describe the old `gh run view --log` behavior instead of the REST/range-fetch implementation.
  WHY: This is a maintainability drift issue that can mislead future edits even though the code path itself has already changed.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2065-2099 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `fetch_log_tail()` only handles the redirect-oriented happy path for the job-logs API, so direct 200 responses or other non-redirect failures return `""` and drop logs.
  WHY: The reviewer reports that the code treats non-301–308 responses as empty tails, so transient API errors or a direct log response lose actionable data instead of surfacing it.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2094-2122 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The outer exception tuple is too narrow and misses `http.client.HTTPException` subclasses such as `IncompleteRead`, allowing a partial log-read failure to abort the Python snapshot writer.
  WHY: When `resp.read()` raises an uncaught HTTP stack exception, the whole heredoc exits non-zero and the shell fallback replaces the snapshot with `writer_error`, losing all check-run data for that iteration.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2094-2122 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: The broad fetch-time exception handling suppresses failures without telemetry, so network/redirect problems are indistinguishable from the intended empty-tail path.
  WHY: The reviewers flagged that transient fetch failures disappear silently, making it hard to tell whether `log_tail` is absent because there was no useful log or because the fetch failed.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2101-2105 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: If the HEAD response omits or mangles `Content-Length`, `fetch_log_tail()` falls back to an empty tail even when the log is otherwise fetchable.
  WHY: The reviewers noted that `int(resp.headers.get("Content-Length", "0"))` collapses missing or malformed values to zero, which silently drops logs instead of attempting a GET fallback.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2108-2120 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The redirect target from the Actions logs API is used directly as `blob_url` for HEAD/GET requests without any scheme or host validation.
  WHY: If that redirect target were ever attacker-controlled, the workflow would follow it blindly; the reviewers judged this low risk because the URL normally comes from GitHub over HTTPS.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2091-2124 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The ranged GET does not enforce that the server actually honored the Range header, so a 200/full-body response gets fully downloaded before truncation.
  WHY: Because `resp.read()` happens before the `_log_tail_bytes` slice, any proxy or backend that ignores Range defeats the bounded-fetch intent and can create unnecessary memory pressure.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2148-2148 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Every failed check-run still incurs the full REST redirect/HEAD/ranged-GET sequence on each autofix iteration.
  WHY: The reviewer flagged this as unnecessary API load and latency, especially when the same stalled or cancelled job is revisited repeatedly.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2094-2094 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The outer except clause does not catch `http.client.HTTPException` subclasses such as `IncompleteRead`, so a partial log read can abort the whole Python snapshot writer.
  WHY: `resp.read()` can raise `IncompleteRead`, and because the exception escapes `fetch_log_tail()`, the shell guard falls back to `writer_error` and drops all check-run data for that iteration.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2109-2121 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The ranged GET path does not verify `206 Partial Content`, so an ignored Range header can cause the full log body to be downloaded before truncation.
  WHY: `resp.read()` loads the body first and only afterward applies `_log_tail_bytes`, which defeats the bounded-fetch intent when the server returns a full 200 response.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2113-2121 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: If the log server ignores the Range header and returns 200 OK, the implementation reads the entire log into memory before truncating it.
  WHY: The post-read slice `out = out[-_log_tail_bytes:]` only runs after `resp.read()` has already loaded all of the data, which defeats the memory-bounding intent.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM mistralai_mistral-small-2603 ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2066-2115 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The `blob_url` from the redirect Location header is used directly for subsequent HEAD/GET requests without validation.
  WHY: A malicious or misconfigured redirect target could send the runner to an unexpected host, enabling SSRF or content injection.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2093-2118 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: If the HEAD response omits or invalidates `Content-Length`, the function returns an empty tail, and if the server ignores Range the whole log is still downloaded.
  WHY: These assumptions can silently drop actionable logs or defeat the byte cap, even though a direct GET might otherwise succeed.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2093-2122 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The broad exception handling suppresses fetch failures without telemetry or cleanup guidance.
  WHY: Transient network or redirect failures become indistinguishable from the intended empty-return path, making debugging much harder.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2053-2053 | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The comments still describe the old `gh run view --log` behavior instead of the new REST/range fetch.
  WHY: That stale documentation can mislead maintainers and increase the chance of future drift.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2047-2050 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The workflow defaults for `CHECK_RUNS_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECS` and `CHECK_RUNS_POLL_INTERVAL_SECS` do not match the README documentation.
  WHY: The reviewer reported `120 vs 1200` and `30 vs 20`, which changes collection timing and makes the implementation stop earlier and poll less frequently than documented.
=== END FINDINGS FROM mistralai_mistral-small-2603 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2079-2091 | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The `blob_url` redirect target is not validated before the workflow issues HEAD/GET requests against it.
  WHY: The reviewer considered this defense-in-depth only, because a compromised redirect or MITM would be needed to exploit it.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2091-2099 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: If the server ignores the Range header and returns 200 OK with the full body, the implementation still downloads the entire log into memory before truncating.
  WHY: That defeats the bounded-fetch intent and can create memory pressure on large job logs.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2101-2104 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: If the HEAD response omits `Content-Length`, the function returns an empty tail instead of trying a direct GET fallback.
  WHY: The reviewer said this can silently drop fetchable logs on backends that do not provide the header.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2094-2095 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The broad `(OSError, ValueError, urllib.error.HTTPError)` catch suppresses network and redirect failures without any telemetry.
  WHY: Operators cannot distinguish a real no-log case from a fetch failure, so debugging empty `log_tail` becomes difficult.
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2108-2120 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The redirect Location header is used as `blob_url` without any scheme or host validation.
  WHY: The reviewer noted that a compromised or unexpected redirect target would then be fetched directly, bypassing any allowlist.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2099-2105 | severity=medium | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: If the logs endpoint ever returns a direct 200 log response instead of a redirect, `fetch_log_tail()` returns `""` and drops the log.
  WHY: The reviewer flagged this as a fragility in the redirect-only assumption, even though the current path is intended to fail open.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2119-2124 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: A Range-ignored 200 response still downloads the full log body before the later truncation.
  WHY: The post-read slice cannot prevent the full transfer, so the byte-cap intent is defeated and large logs can pressure the runner.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2101-2105 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A missing or malformed `Content-Length` on the HEAD response collapses the fetch to an empty tail.
  WHY: The reviewer said this causes fetchable logs to be silently dropped, and also noted that blob requests omit a `User-Agent`.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2108-2120 | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The blob HEAD/GET requests are accepted without any explicit validation of the returned URL or response shape.
  WHY: The reviewer treated this as hardening-only and noted that malformed header values can also collapse the fetch path to zero-length output.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===

=== FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2065-2099 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The initial `/actions/jobs/{job_id}/logs` fetch only works for explicit redirects, so non-redirect HTTP errors and transient failures immediately return `""`.
  WHY: The reviewer said this makes common API failures indistinguishable from an empty-summary case and recreates the “no actionable log_tail” problem.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2109-2122 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The ranged GET can still download the full log body into memory if the server ignores the Range header.
  WHY: The later truncation cannot limit the transfer, so large logs can still OOM or blow the reviewer/editor prompt budget.
